source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: SK Hynix should replicate Nvidia's credit wrapper / revenue share model to capture upside from the AI compute buildout
summary_extended: Baker argues that SK Hynix should adopt Nvidia's credit wrapper / revenue share financing model to capture a larger share of the AI compute buildout's economics. Specifically, he says that if he were CEO of SK Hynix, he would approach GPU buyers and offer to put up cash as surety upfront in exchange for a cut of ongoing revenues — mirroring the structure Nvidia is reportedly using to help customers finance Blackwell/Rubin purchases amid a ~$700B credit gap. His reasoning is that memory companies like SK Hynix and Micron now have strong cash flows and credit markets are tightening, creating an opportune moment for suppliers to offer alternative financing structures that also give them revenue upside. He notes that Blackstone and Apollo are likely already pitching variants of this to hyperscalers, suggesting the window for memory companies to act is now. The investment implication is that Micron (the US-listed HBM producer) could pursue a similar strategy, potentially transforming its earnings profile from a commodity cyclical to a revenue-share participant in AI infrastructure.
